subject: Mode selection playbook for Quantico AI — follow-up on latency / throughput
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Harper <elliot.harper@quantico.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mode selection playbook for Quantico AI — follow-up on latency / throughput

Hi Elliot — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on Hosted vs Dedicated for your inference path. TL;DR: we need a short traffic sample and your target p50/p95 so we can run a proof-of-performance and recommend a deployment.

Recap from the call:
- Primary workload: assistant completions for GenAI search (average completion length ~80 tokens, some up to 512).
- Current model: quantized vicuna-13b (you mentioned a 4-bit build).
- Business target: sub-200ms p95 for short queries (<=128 tokens), and <300ms p95 for longer completions. Peak concurrent QPS estimate was "~25 QPS" with burst to ~60 during event windows.

Preliminary guidance (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest path to prod and cheapest to start. Good if your sustained QPS is under ~10-15 and you can tolerate regional multi-tenant variance. Not ideal as a single source for strict p95 SLOs at sustained 25 QPS.
- Dedicated capacity: recommended if you need predictable p95/p50 at sustained >20 QPS or if you want strict isolation for burst-to-peak traffic. Gives fixed GPU pools, autoscaling policies, and SLA-backed latency targets.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): overkill at this stage unless you have hard residency or audit requirements; we can discuss later if SOC2/HIPAA constraints push you that way.

What we need from you to finalize recommendation and a cost/time estimate:
1) Sample traffic trace (anonymized): distribution of prompt lengths, tokens per request, per-minute QPS for a 24–72 hour window. CSV is fine.
2) Clear latency targets: p50/p95 goals for short (<=128 tokens) and long (>128 tokens) completions.
3) Which model variant(s) to validate (e.g., vicuna-13b q4/q5).

Proposed next steps:
- You send the traffic sample + confirm p95 targets (you can reply inline).
- We run a 48-hour PoP (proof-of-performance) on a dedicated-like sandbox: measure p50/p95 and throughput characteristics.
- Based on results we’ll scope Dedicated pool size and autoscale policy; if Hosted meets SLOs we’ll document cost delta.

Attachments: please attach a 24–72h traffic sample and any security checklist items (you mentioned a short PDF). I attached a template below for reference.

Thanks — I'll coordinate with Neha/Karthik on the perf plan once we have the sample.

— Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

Attachment stubs: traffic-sample-template.csv (CSV stub), hosted-vs-dedicated-one-pager.pdf (stub)

From: Elliot Harper <elliot.harper@quantico.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@quantico.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 18:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mode selection playbook for Quantico AI — follow-up on latency / throughput

Thanks, Stephanie — useful recap. Quick answers below and I've attached a short sample export.

Answers:
- Traffic sample attached: traffic-sample-20270419.csv (24h export, anonymized user ids). Peak minute ~25 QPS, sustained 12–18 QPS across business hours. Bursts up to ~60 QPS for push notifications.
- Latency targets: p50 < 80ms (short <=128 tokens), p95 < 150ms (short); for longer completions (>128) p95 target is 300ms but we can accept up to 400ms if necessary.
- Model variant: vicuna-13b q4_0 (4-bit) for primary; experimenting with q5 later.

Open questions for you: if Dedicated is recommended, can you give a rough lead time for provisioning a dedicated pool (we're evaluating timeline for a May launch)? Also, what sort of delta should we expect in cost vs Hosted for our profile?

I attached our security questionnaire — happy to sign an NDA if helpful.

Best,
Elliot
Head of Product | Quantico AI
elliot.harper@quantico.ai

Attachment: traffic-sample-20270419.csv (CSV), quantico-security-questions.pdf (PDF)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 07:22:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Mode selection playbook for Quantico AI — follow-up on latency / throughput

Stephanie / Karthik — quick technical read of Elliot's sample and my recommended approach. Quoting the key line from Elliot: "Peak minute ~25 QPS, sustained 12–18 QPS, bursts up to ~60 QPS."

Notes / recommendation:
- Quant profile: vicuna-13b q4_0; median tokens/request ~80; tail to 512. Good to note the quantized model will change memory/throughput characteristics vs fp16.
- Baseline: if they need p95 <150ms for short queries at sustained ~20+ QPS, Hosted tier is unlikely to guarantee that reliably during bursts. Dedicated pool is the correct path for their pro-SLA target.

Suggested Dedicated sizing (initial guess):
- Start with a 3-node pool of A100-equivalent GPUs (or our equivalent dense inference machines) with continuous batching and a conservative autoscale policy (scale up at 60% CPU/GPU utilization, scale down slowly). This covers sustained 20–25 QPS and headroom for bursts with burst capacity enabled.
- Autoscale config: min 2 nodes, target 3 nodes, burst reserve +2 nodes for event windows.

PoP/test plan (things we need to run):
1) Replay their 24h trace at 2x speed to surface queueing and p95 under stress.
2) Single-client p95/kv-cache warm vs cold runs for short (<=128) and long (>128) completions.
3) Measure token throughput and per-request tail latencies with streaming enabled.

Data / actions required from sales side:
- Confirm whether Quantico expects multi-region routing for DR (they did not say) — if yes, Dedicated cross-region config changes sizing.
- Confirm acceptance of a short PoP agreement (we run tests in sandbox, results shared, no charge for 48h PoP but we require signed PoP acceptance).

Estimated timeline: provisioning Dedicated sandbox (for PoP) = 2–3 business days after we have the signed PoP agreement and model artifacts. Full production Dedicated pool provisioning = 5–7 business days post-SOW.

I'll draft a minimal PoP agreement template we can send. Also linking our internal perf runbook for reference: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1InternalRunbookExample (internal).

— Neha
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.com

2) Quantico: sign the attached PoP acceptance (I’ll send the short doc via DocuSign). We need this to provision the sandbox. (Owner: Elliot)
3) Redwood: Neha will spin up the 48h PoP sandbox and run the replay + tail tests once PoP is signed and model artifact is uploaded to our secure bucket. Expected start = within 2–3 business days of signature. (Owner: Neha)
4) Redwood: I’ll create a HubSpot deal + SOW draft with preliminary Dedicated sizing and cost delta vs Hosted (link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/7890). (Owner: Stephanie)

Scheduling: I propose we target PoP kickoff the week of Apr 26 (depending on signatures). Can you confirm availability for a short kickoff call (30m) next Tue/Wed?

I'll also attach a one-pager that summarizes Dedicated vs Hosted for calls with your leadership.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this validated quickly.
